assessment: Revision 5 requires pending effect cycles to block new Q/P before forwarding, validates lexical statuses before release, and associates completion with ordered Q/Sync barriers. The abstract policy proves pending and forward blocking, invalid completion retention, older effect removal and newer effect retention, with a concrete witness.
implementation_acceptance_notes: Cycle identifier assignment and ReadyForQuery-to-barrier association must correctly model actual ordered Q/Sync protocol, including E before Sync and an older Ready after a newer E.
Set pending before forwarding Q/E; reject later Q/P while pending, yet permit required progress messages and validate all intervening ParameterStatus before release.
Exercise indirect pg_settings changes and delayed and fragmented responses; ensure denial precedes backend receipt.
Do not claim Python, wire framing, parser adapter, database behavior or GUC validation are proved by this Lean model.
formal_limits: The cycle model is separate from the prepared-routing model; sourceAllowed denotes the shared Q/P gate abstractly. Natural-number cycle ordering and matching acknowledgement are adapter assumptions, not protocol correspondence proofs.
